title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & cost breakdown - Verdant Retail
next_steps: Send detailed pricing sheet and sample billing export
Share SOC2 and security pack link
Provision trial Dedicated capacity for 2-week benchmark
Schedule integration call with Verdant DevOps (Jordan) next Wed 12/23
action_items: Alex - Send pricing + billing example by 2026-12-17
Samir - Share benchmark runbook and request form by 2026-12-18
Priya - Add Verdant to pilot onboarding queue and introduce CSM by 2026-12-18
Jordan - Provide typical daily QPS and top 10 routes by 2026-12-18
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex Martinez from Redwood here, Samir our SE and Priya on CSM. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Maya (Verdant): Hi Alex, good thanks. Excited to see the console stuff. We've been looking at your docs but want to see per-route cost in action.
[00:15] Samir (SE): Great, we'll walk through the Redwood Consol — sorry, Console — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown flows. I'll share my screen and start in the Analytics tab.
[00:28] Jordan (DevOps): Cool. Also we'll flag our main ask: can we get a Dedicated pilot and run some runs against our top routes?
[00:34] Alex: Totally. We'll cover that — and there's a benchmark runbook we'll send.
[00:40] [Screenshare starts] Samir: Ok, here is the top-level Usage Overview. You can see tokens in, tokens out, average latency, error rate, and cost estimates. Note these are modeled — real billing is slightly different but we surface a token-level cost estimate tied to routes.
[01:05] Liam (CTO): That cost estimate — is that per-model, per-route? How do you attribute shared models across multiple routes?
[01:12] Samir: Good q. We attribute by route tag, so when you call /api/generate-sales-summary it maps to that route and we calculate per-route token consumption, plus host overhead. If multiple routes use the same model instance, we split by request count and tokens. It's an estimation but in practice aligns within 3-8% to real invoices.
[01:32] Maya: We have a lot of bursty traffic — Black Friday spikes. How does batching and autoscaling show up here?
[01:38] Samir: We surface batching efficiency as a separate metric; the console shows time-of-day histograms and batching rate. For Dedicated you can also see reserved pool utilization and burst capacity usage.
[01:50] [01:50] Samir: Switching over to Per-Route Dashboard for your top 5 routes.
[01:55] Samir: Here we have route metrics — QPS, p50/p95 latency, token breakdown by prompt vs completion, and cost split: compute, memory (KV cache hotness), and infra egress. You can click into the 7-day view or a custom range.
[02:12] Jordan: The KV cache line — we saw a note about K-V cache earlier — what is 'KV cache hotness'?
[02:18] Samir: Yeah K-V cache hotness is how often the model's key-value cache hits on repeated prefixes; higher hotness reduces repeated compute. We show hit rate and estimated token savings. Sometimes transcript labels show as K-V or kv cache, the real metric name in the API is kv_cache_hit_rate.
[02:35] Maya: There's a small typo in the console: 'cache' shows as 'cash' in one of our demo flows, we laughed.
[02:40] Alex: We'll file that UI bug.
[02:44] [03:00] Samir: Now the Cost Breakdown drawer — you can open a route and see a waterfall: model compute (per-token), batching gains (negative), quantization savings, and routing overheads when we fall back to cheaper variants.
[03:18] Samir: For example, if you run the 'product-recommend-v2' route on a 16k context LLM vs a 4k variant, the per-token compute delta is visible and we show an estimated monthly cost at current usage.
[03:33] Liam: Can we tie this to our finance systems? We need a CSV export or API endpoint.
[03:39] Samir: Yes, there's a billing export; a CSV and also an API endpoint that returns per-route cost daily aggregates. I'll drop the link to the sample export after the call.
[03:50] Priya (CSM): Link: https://redwood.ai/decks/verdant-demo (we'll also attach the sample billing csv).
[03:58] [04:10] Maya: About SSO and audit logs — we need to know who ran what and when for compliance.
[04:16] Alex: We have audit logs in the Console, and we integrate with your SAML IdP for SSO provisioning. Logs include route, user, timestamp, and request id. For Private deployments you can route logs to your SIEM.
[04:31] Jordan: Does the audit include payload? That's the ask from security — PII concerns.
[04:37] Samir: By default we log metadata only; payload logging is off. If you enable payload capture in a Private deployment you can choose redaction options or send it to your KMS-protected store.
[04:52] Maya: Good. Also SOC 2 — we need docs.
[04:57] Alex: We'll send SOC2, ISO certs and our security pack in the follow-up.
[05:05] [05:20] Samir: Back to dashboards — here's the Anomaly Detection pane. It raises regressions on latency and generation quality tied to eval prompt sets. If a route deviates, we create an alert and tie it to recent model rollouts.
[05:36] Maya: Can we create alerts for cost thresholds? E.g., stop rollout if cost per 1M tokens > $X.
[05:42] Samir: Yes, you can create policy-based alerts on any metric including cost per token or monthly spend per route. We also have automatic rollback policies if a canary exceeds cost or latency budgets.
[05:55] Liam: About canaries — do you support weighted traffic splits?
[06:00] Samir: Yes, canary traffic splits (1-10%) with automatic rollback or manual promotion. We also store per-canary metrics.
[06:08] [06:30] Alex: Quick qualification — what's your timeline and success criteria for a pilot?
[06:35] Maya: We want to run a 2-week pilot in January, see 20% cost improvement versus our current setup and maintain p95 latency under 300ms. We also need private networking (VPC peering) for some of our traffic.
[06:50] Alex: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose Dedicated pilot with VPC peering and reserved pool sized to your typical baseline traffic.
[06:58] Jordan: For the Dedicated pilot, how do we measure exact savings? We want apples-to-apples.
[07:04] Samir: We instrument the runbook to capture pre- and post- metrics: tokens, latency, p95, batching efficiency, kv cache hit rate, per-route cost. We'll give you a spreadsheet. We'll also run side-by-side inference if you can route a subset of traffic.
[07:20] [07:40] Samir: Now I'll demo the Alerts & Reports builder. You can create a scheduled cost report that emails finance with top routes and cost drivers.
[07:50] Elena (Product): Nice. Can we add custom tags to routes for team-level chargebacks?
[07:55] Samir: Absolutely. Routes support tags and we have a dimension called 'business_unit' so finance can break down cost.
[08:05] Maya: Any integrations with DataDog or Splunk for metrics/traces?
[08:10] Samir: We have outbound metrics via StatsD/Prometheus and traces via OpenTelemetry. Also webhook hooks for alerts.
[08:20] [08:35] Liam: On security — KMS/HSM support? Key rotation?
[08:40] Samir: Yes for Private deployments we support KMS-based envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys, and rotation policies. Hosted plans have customer-managed keys via an integration too.
[08:52] [09:10] Samir: Jumping to the Optimize tab briefly — here's our recommendations engine. Given your route profiles it suggests quantization levels and batching windows to reduce cost while staying within latency SLO.
[09:25] Samir: Example: recommending 4-bit quantization for the 'intent-classify' route yielded estimated 30% compute reduction with little quality impact. We surface a confidence score and test prompts to validate.
[09:40] Maya: Do recommendations include model variant switches?
[09:44] Samir: Yes, switch suggestions show delta in both cost and expected p95 latency. You can preview a canary that routes 5% traffic to the cheaper variant.
[09:55] [10:05] Jordan: If we switch to a quantized model, do you manage the model bits/precision or do we need to produce the quantized artifact?
[10:12] Samir: We provide both: we host Redwood-verified quantized variants for common open models, or we can take your artifact and run through our quantization pipeline in a controlled pilot.
[10:25] [10:40] Maya: About fallbacks — for graceful degradation, how does Redwood handle spikes when Dedicated pool is saturated?
[10:46] Samir: Policy-based routing will fall back to a cheaper hosted variant in a different region or queue requests with a best-effort SLA. You can configure strict fail-open vs fail-closed behaviors.
[11:00] Liam: Any egress cost surprises when we use cross-region fallbacks?
[11:05] Samir: The Cost Breakdown highlights cross-region egress and you can set policies to avoid fallback to regions with high egress.
[11:12] [11:30] Alex: Quick check — competitors. Any particular RFP items you're comparing?
[11:35] Maya: We're also evaluating Anthropic and Vertex for managed endpoints. Key differentiators for us are cost transparency and predictable Dedicated pricing.
[11:43] Alex: Understood — we find our per-route dashboards and built-in cost attribution help finance teams a lot.
[11:50] [12:05] Samir: Jumping to Live Traces — here's a single request flow: request id, route, tokens used, model variant, server hops, and a small snippet of the prompt hash (not full content) for traceability.
[12:20] Jordan: Good that prompt content isn't logged by default. We need retention policies on logs too.
[12:25] Samir: Retention configurable per-tenant and per-log type; we can set short retention for metadata and longer for audit logs.
[12:36] [12:55] Samir: Now the Reports section — scheduled weekly spend by team, and a drilldown to top 10 cost drivers.
[13:05] Elena: Can this drive automated chargebacks to our internal ledger?
[13:09] Samir: We have an API so you can pull daily aggregates; a webhook option to push into your finance system is also available.
[13:20] [13:40] Maya: On compliance again, if we go Private, do we get a separate control plane?
[13:45] Alex: Yes Private deployments can have a customer-managed control plane and on-prem option for air-gapped environments.
[13:52] [14:10] Samir: I'm going to show a quick canary rollout: we set route tags, create a canary with 5% traffic, attach an alert on p95 and cost-per-10k-tokens, then promote or rollback.
[14:25] Maya: Nice UX. How are audits stored for rollouts?
[14:30] Samir: Every rollout has a changelog with who triggered it, timestamp, exact config, and diff.
[14:38] [15:00] Alex: Ok, time to align on next steps. Recap from our side: we'll send pricing and the SOC2/security pack, Samir will share the benchmark runbook and billing export sample, Priya will onboard you to the pilot queue, and Jordan will share daily QPS and top routes.
[15:18] Maya: We'll aim to get the QPS and routes by Friday.
[15:22] Liam: We'll confirm pilot scope and sign an NDA if required.
[15:26] Alex: Sounds good. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the integration call next Wed.
[15:33] Priya: Noted, I'll send the invite.
[15:36] [15:45] Samir: I'll also attach a short demo recording and the links: security pack (https://redwood.ai/security/pack) and benchmark runbook (https://redwood.ai/runbooks/benchmarks).
[15:55] Maya: Thanks, this was helpful.
[16:00] Alex: Thanks everybody — we'll be in touch.
[16:03] [End of recording]
